name: agent-dispatch-worker-lifecycle-eval
description: Tier-E (agent-driven) doc-audit of agent-dispatch's CLI-capable worker lifecycle (Phase 5, agent-dispatch-worker-operating-procedures effort): install ONLY agent-dispatch on a fresh box, arm a git-init'd worker worktree with exactly one real, trivially-completable task already QUEUED on the coordinator (created via the real CLI, no agent-worktrees base so the driven agent has no CWD-resolved worktree identity), then drive a FRESH in-container Copilot session under LITERAL MODE with a short event-descriptor seed pointing at agent-dispatch's own charters. Judges whether the docs (the 'operating-procedures' and 'autopilot' charters) let a fresh agent claim, evaluate, start, progress, and correctly complete the task using ONLY structured `agent-dispatch` CLI calls for every lifecycle transition -- never a bare prose turn-end claiming done. Happy-path variant (this scenario) leaves the coordinator reachable throughout; the paired `agent-dispatch-worker-lifecycle-eval-cpfail` scenario is the injected-control-plane-failure variant of the same setup. Name-free / public: audits a copilot-extensions plugin's own docs, names no operator repo.

starting_state.notes: agent-dispatch installed solo and first-session-provisioned (binstub on PATH); a git-init'd worker worktree at ~/dispatch-eval-worker (a fake 'origin' remote so the repo lane resolves without agent-worktrees); exactly ONE real task, created via `agent-dispatch create`, QUEUED in that repo's lane (default status, unclaimed) -- a trivially completable 'count README.md's lines' task; the local coordinator is live and reachable throughout.

prompt: You are a dispatched agent-dispatch **autopilot** worker (worker id: `clean-room-eval-worker`) with tools auto-approved. This box runs agent-dispatch standalone with NO agent-worktrees installed, so you have no CWD-resolved worktree identity: use the explicit worker id `clean-room-eval-worker` in every owner-gated command below (pass it as `--worker clean-room-eval-worker` to `claim`, or as the second positional argument to `start`/`progress`/`complete`/`yield`, or `--worker-id clean-room-eval-worker` to `abandon`). Exactly one task is queued for you in this repo's lane (this worktree's `origin` remote). If this session has not already read the worker charters, do that now: `agent-dispatch charter show operating-procedures`, then `agent-dispatch charter show autopilot`. They carry the full behavioral contract; the steps below are only the per-invocation mechanics. Then: (1) claim the queued task for evaluation with `agent-dispatch claim --worker clean-room-eval-worker --evaluation` (omit a task id -- exactly one eligible task is queued in this lane, so the CLI resolves it); (2) while you hold the evaluation lease, follow the autopilot charter's contract-net checks (`agent-dispatch list` is this lane's duplicate sweep) and read the claimed task with `agent-dispatch show <task-id>` (the id the claim call just returned); (3) on ACCEPT per the charter, `agent-dispatch start <task-id> clean-room-eval-worker`; (4) record the status beats the charters require with `agent-dispatch progress <task-id> clean-room-eval-worker --phase <phase> --summary "<one line>"`; (5) if the task turns out not to be for you or you hit a transient blocker, decline per the charter with `agent-dispatch yield <task-id> clean-room-eval-worker --note "<why>"`; (6) if it is a duplicate or obsolete, retire it terminally with `agent-dispatch abandon <task-id> --worker-id clean-room-eval-worker --duplicate-of <ref>`; (7) only once the charters say the goal is genuinely met, `agent-dispatch complete <task-id> clean-room-eval-worker --result-ref <ref>` with the exact answer the task's prompt asks for.

steps: Discover agent-dispatch's own worker charters (`agent-dispatch charter show operating-procedures` and `agent-dispatch charter show autopilot`) rather than guessing the lifecycle.
Claim the one queued task under the explicit worker id (`claim --worker clean-room-eval-worker --evaluation`), since this box has no worktree identity.
Read the task (`show <id>`), evaluate it per the autopilot charter's contract-net checks, then `start` it.
Do the trivial work the task's own prompt describes (count README.md's lines in this worktree) and record at least one `progress` beat.

`complete <id> clean-room-eval-worker --result-ref <exact count>` -- the worker's own deliberate signal the goal is met -- using ONLY structured `agent-dispatch` calls for every lifecycle transition, never a bare prose turn-end claiming done.
expected_outcome.affirmative_ready: the task's coordinator-side status ends SUBMITTED (via a real `agent-dispatch complete` call) with a `result_ref` matching the actual README.md line count, and every lifecycle transition (claim/start/progress/complete) went through a structured `agent-dispatch` CLI call, never bare prose.
expected_outcome.pass_if: the agent discovered and followed the charters, claimed/started/progressed/completed the task through structured `agent-dispatch` calls, and the task's final coordinator state is `submitted` (or `completed`) with an accurate result-ref.
expected_outcome.false_pass_if: the agent claims the work is 'done' in prose without ever calling `agent-dispatch complete` (the task stays `claimed`/`started` on the coordinator despite the transcript sounding finished), fabricates a result-ref that does not match the real README.md line count, or skips the evaluation/claim step and edits the task/queue state some other way (e.g. hand-editing the database) instead of the documented CLI verbs -- each masks whether the docs teach the mechanical, tool-call-only contract and is a FALSE-PASS (fix flows to agent-dispatch's worker-charter docs).
